contrasts.title: The verb comes second
contrasts.body: In a Norwegian main clause the verb is always the second element. If you start with a time or place, the subject moves after the verb: «I dag er det min første dag», not «I dag det er…».

contrasts.title: «Halv tolv» is 11:30
contrasts.body: Norwegian counts half an hour towards the next hour. «Halv tolv» means 11:30, not 12:30 as British «half twelve» would.

itemNotes.a2-fdw-02: «Sjef» looks like «chef», but it means boss.
itemNotes.a2-fdw-03: «Halv tolv» is half an hour before twelve: 11:30.
itemNotes.a2-fdw-11: After the verb, use the object pronoun: jeg (I) → meg (me).
itemNotes.a2-fdw-13: The sentence starts with «I dag», so the verb «er» comes next, then the subject «det».
itemNotes.a2-fdw-15: After «fordi» (because) the order is subject, then verb: «kollegene er».
